statements.quote: As AI and other technologies advance, it is important that we preserve the integrity of constituent interactions. This legislation will ensure that Americans’ voices are not drowned out by automated content generated by bad actors.
statements.context: Higgins reintroduced H.R. 9643, the Comment Integrity and Management Act, requiring federal agencies to verify that public comments on rules are submitted by humans.
statements.reason: About AI-generated comments flooding federal rulemaking, with no acknowledgment of catastrophic risk.

statements.venue: House Oversight Committee hearing (as reported by MeriTalk)
statements.quote: It’s the moratorium that’s asking the states to recognize that AI, by nature, is interstate commerce,
statements.context: Higgins defended the proposed 10-year moratorium on state enforcement of AI laws in the 2025 budget bill.
statements.reason: About federal preemption of state AI laws, with no acknowledgment of catastrophic risk.

slowdown.note: No statement found on slowing frontier AI development. His 2025 support for a moratorium on state AI law enforcement is about regulation, not slowing AI, so it does not count.

pause.note: No statement found on pausing frontier AI development.

record: Reintroduced H.R. 9643, the Comment Integrity and Management Act, requiring agencies to verify that public comments come from humans, citing AI-generated comment floods.
grade_reason: His AI remarks since January 2025 are about AI-generated comments in federal rulemaking (July 2026) and support for the 2025 moratorium on state AI law enforcement; neither acknowledges catastrophic risk. No A, B, C or F statement was found in 2025 or 2026.
notes: All 6 required web searches ran this time, plus one more checking House co-sponsors of the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (7 in total). No source showed Higgins sponsoring or co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538); listed House co-sponsors in search results did not include him, though those lists conflicted, so congress.gov was not checked directly. No House letter on AI risk signed by him was found. From the earlier attempt: his official newsroom pages 1 to 3 (press releases from 2 October 2025 to 12 November 2026) were opened directly and, besides the 16 July 2026 release, none concerned AI; the 2026 quote was checked against that page's HTML. The June 2025 quote was checked against the MeriTalk page's HTML; the same article paraphrases him as saying states remain free to pass their own AI laws while the federal government requests a pause on enforcement (paraphrase, left out). Outside the time window: a 10 September 2023 press release (https://clayhiggins.house.gov/media/press-releases/higgins-introduce-legislation-banning-government-weaponization-artificial) quotes him saying "AI is an Armageddon level threat, far more ominous than any alleged pandemic or climate crisis," in the context of opposing federal government use of AI for law enforcement. It is from before 2025, so it is left out of statements and does not affect the grade; a reviewer may still want to know about it. Searches on superintelligence, extinction, and China agreements returned nothing mentioning him. A 2025 House hearing transcript (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CHRG-119hhrg60818/html/CHRG-119hhrg60818.htm) appeared in results but was not opened.
